patches.value: Recorded live at a Simchas Beis Hashoeva rally for children during Sukkos 5786. Rabbi Goldstein welcomes the crowd and jokes with Simcha Engel about the new year, then groups of children come up to recite the Twelve Pesukim, and everyone says and sings Al Tira together. Rabbi Goldstein explains that tonight's Ushpizin, Yaakov Avinu and the Alter Rebbe, both excelled in learning Torah, and tells a story of the Alter Rebbe. The Alter Rebbe arrives for the wedding of two orphans whose match he had made, only to find that the town official has seized the groom to send him to the Russian army for twenty-five years. The official demands 1,500 rubles, and the poor town cannot raise even half. With Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev and Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Horodok, the Alter Rebbe visits the richest man in town, known for giving only a nickel. He accepts the nickel with a smile and a warm brachah, and the man keeps calling them back with more, until he breaks down, tells why he had stopped giving tzedakah, and pays the whole ransom. The wedding goes ahead with great joy, and the evening ends with a lesson about reaching every Jew's heart.
patches.reason: Host re-attributed to R' Chaim Levi Goldstein; 'Uncle Yossi' (his father) is not said on air here, the host is called 'Rabbi Goldstein'.

patches.value: Recorded live at a Simchas Beis Hashoeva rally for children during Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5786, on the night of the Rebbe Maharash and his motto 'Lechatchila Ariber'. Simcha Engel turns up with a shoe missing: he danced so hard he lost it, after hearing the Rebbe's teaching that joyful dancing now can make up for whatever was missed earlier in the season. Rabbi Goldstein lists the Ushpizin and explains that tonight's guests, Yosef HaTzaddik and the Rebbe Maharash, teach that a Jew can leap straight to the greatest heights, just as Yosef went from prison to ruler at once. He then begins a story of a Jewish innkeeper whose village priest wants to drive him out of business. The story pauses while groups of children recite the Twelve Pesukim and Al Tira. When it resumes, the priest pretends to make peace, swaps in a poisoned bottle, and blames the innkeeper when a customer dies. The Rebbe Maharash puts off seeing him for two days, then sends him straight home on a first-class train ticket, where he unknowingly pours out his heart to the very judges of his case. They uncover the priest's plot and the innkeeper goes free.

patches.value: Recorded live at a Simchas Beis Hashoeva rally for children on the night of Hoshana Rabbah. Rabbi Goldstein wishes everyone a good and sweet year and explains that tonight's Ushpizin, Dovid HaMelech and the Rebbe Rashab, are both connected to Moshiach. A child character arrives with a Tehillim and a Chumash, ready for the Hoshana Rabbah custom of reading Sefer Devarim and saying Tehillim, and asks whether to say it with tears as in the olden days. Rabbi Goldstein explains that the Rebbe taught our generation to serve Hashem with simcha and bitachon, and tells a story: in the time of the Tzemach Tzedek, a Chassid whose son was gravely ill traveled to Lubavitch and received only 'Hashem should help you'. He spent Hoshana Rabbah crying over Tehillim, then decided to dance with all his might through Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah. Before he left, the Tzemach Tzedek told him that his joy had broken a Heavenly decree and his son would recover. Rabbi Goldstein closes with the Zohar's teaching that Heaven gives according to the joy on our faces, and the Rebbe's call to grab another Jew while dancing and bring Moshiach. The emcee then begins the Twelve Pesukim.
